title: Words, Truth, and Reputation
subtitle: A person’s words can build trust, settle conflict, or damage a reputation that took years to establish.
author: Murle Connect Editorial Team
proverb: A spoken word cannot be gathered back after it has been released.
summary: This proverb teaches that speech carries great responsibility. Words can create friendship, preserve peace, communicate truth, and strengthen trust, but careless, false, or angry words can damage relationships and reputations. The proverb encourages people to think carefully before speaking and to value honesty, restraint, and accountability.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Words are among the most powerful tools human beings possess. They can comfort someone who is suffering, encourage a child, resolve a disagreement, preserve history, or bring people together. However, words can also insult, accuse, divide families, spread rumors, and create conflict. This proverb reminds people that speech should never be treated as something harmless or without consequences.

sections.heading: Meaning
sections.content: Once words have been spoken publicly, they may travel far beyond the speaker’s control. Even if a person later apologizes or denies what was said, others may continue remembering the original statement. The proverb therefore teaches people to think before speaking, especially when angry, afraid, jealous, or under pressure. Truthful and careful speech builds trust, while careless speech can destroy relationships that took many years to develop.

sections.heading: Traditional Story
sections.content: A young man once spread an accusation about another member of his community without confirming whether it was true. The rumor quickly moved from one household to another and caused tension between families. Later, the young man discovered that the accusation was false. He apologized, but the damage had already been done because people had begun to distrust one another. An elder told him that feathers released into the wind cannot easily be collected again. The story taught him that words, like feathers in the wind, can travel beyond anyone’s ability to retrieve them.

sections.heading: Lesson
sections.content: The proverb teaches truthfulness, self-control, responsibility, and respect. People should avoid gossip, exaggeration, false accusations, and promises they cannot keep. Speaking honestly does not mean speaking harshly. A wise person knows how to tell the truth with fairness and compassion. The proverb also teaches that apologies are important, but prevention is better than causing harm through careless speech.

sections.heading: Modern Application
sections.content: This lesson is especially important in the age of mobile phones, social media, messaging platforms, and online communities. A rumor can now spread to thousands of people within minutes. False information can damage someone’s reputation, create fear, or provoke conflict. Young people should verify information before sharing it and should remember that online words can have real consequences. Leaders, journalists, teachers, and ordinary citizens all have a responsibility to communicate truthfully.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Words should be treated as valuable and dangerous at the same time. They can heal wounds or deepen them, create peace or encourage conflict, and establish trust or destroy it. The proverb reminds people to speak with wisdom, verify information, control anger, and understand that reputation is built slowly but can be damaged quickly. Responsible speech is one of the foundations of peaceful community life.

moral: Think carefully before speaking because words cannot always be taken back once they have caused harm.
reflection: Have your words ever helped someone or hurt someone, and what did that experience teach you?
